entities.summary:
Count Axel Otto Mörner (1774-06-08, Lekaryds församling - 1852-10-20) was a Swedish artist and general.

As a prominent Swedish military leader during the Swedish Empire's conflicts with Napoleon's France, Mörner played a key role in the Battle of Stralsund (1808) and the Battle of Riga (1813).

Mörner's artistic talents were recognized in Sweden, and he created various works, including oil paintings, watercolors, and sketches. His artwork is now preserved in several museums, including the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm.

Mörner's legacy extends to his contributions to the Swedish military and art world, influencing future generations of Swedish artists and military leaders.

The devastating consequences of the Battle of Stralsund, which resulted in the loss of thousands of lives and widespread destruction, would forever change the face of Sweden and its people.
